transcript: did you know there's a pirate musical performed on an actual historic boat? I had my own little maritime adventure taking the NYC Ferry to Red Hook, Brooklyn to catch The Royal Pyrate performed on the Lehigh Valley Barge No. 79 which is over 100 years old and maintained by the Waterfront Barge Museum and the musical itself is inspired by the infamous true story of the pirates Sam Bellamy and Blackbeard the show is very music-forward with songs that blend different genres from sea shanties to soft rock while also telling this story that's inspired by real history but also reflecting themes that are still relevant today the show starts off with a bit of a silly, campy vibe complete with pirate-themed puns but as it goes along it reveals itself to be a bit of an “eat the rich” narrative exploring the struggle between democracy and tyranny everywhere from the systems of government to the way that a pirate captain leads his crew at the early performance that I attended I did find, personally that the show got a little bit weighed down by the more somber, emotional tone as it went along in a way that sometimes got in the way of the pacing and the clarity of storytelling but there's still a lot to like about it and as someone who does tend to enjoy these sort of nautical piratey vibes the show definitely delivers on that experience complete with sword fights, adventures and search for treasure so if this sounds up your alley and if you're up for a voyage into Red Hook the Royal Pyrate is running for a couple more weekends through August 31st
